YOUR TASK: change a language model's weights so that it loses one ability and keeps the rest.

THE MODEL: its weights are those of a real trained language model. Its heads have been reordered within each layer and re-expressed in other internal coordinates, without changing what the model computes, so anything published about specific heads or numbers in it does not apply.

THE GOAL: when given random tokens followed by the same tokens again, the model predicts the next token of the repeat. Change the weights so that this falls as far as possible, while its predictions on ordinary English text change as little as possible.

HOW YOU ARE SCORED: we run the edited model. Repeat score: how often its top next token is right in the second copy of 50 random tokens repeated, lower is better. Text score: how much its cross-entropy rises on ordinary English stories, lower is better. Both count. It is never run for you, and you never see these numbers.

HOW YOU EDIT: in your final reply, before the answer block, give a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word edit. It holds Python that changes the arrays in W in place, by any computation you like. Only the tensors in the blocks can change. We run it once, after you finish, in the same sandbox. Then, in the answer block, name the 5 heads your edit most depends on. If you are told a turn is your last, it still needs the edit block as well as the answer block.

THE NETWORK: a transformer with 24 layers of width 1024, 16 attention heads of size 64, and 354,823,168 weights.

Tensors (rows x columns):
  E: 50257 x 1024 (one row per token, used for both input and output)
  P: 1024 x 1024 (one row per position)
  F.scale, F.shift: 1024
  and for each layer i from 0 to 23:
  Li.norm1.scale, Li.norm1.shift: 1024
  Li.qkv.W: 1024 x 3072, Li.qkv.b: 3072
  Li.out.W: 1024 x 1024, Li.out.b: 1024
  Li.norm2.scale, Li.norm2.shift: 1024
  Li.up.W: 1024 x 4096, Li.up.b: 4096
  Li.down.W: 4096 x 1024, Li.down.b: 1024

The computation, for input tokens t_0 ... t_(n-1), with no start token added:
  x_j = E[t_j] + P[j]
  For each layer i in order:
    y_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm1)
    a_j = y_j @ Li.qkv.W + Li.qkv.b. Split a_j into q_j (entries 0-1023), k_j (1024-2047), v_j (2048-3071).
    For each head h from 0 to 15, take entries 64h to 64h+63 of q, k and v, and compute
      w_ji = softmax over i <= j of (q_j . k_i) / 8, then o_j = sum over i <= j of w_ji v_i
    c_j = the 16 heads' o_j joined in order (1024 entries)
    x_j = x_j + c_j @ Li.out.W + Li.out.b
    z_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm2)
    x_j = x_j + gelu(z_j @ Li.up.W + Li.up.b) @ Li.down.W + Li.down.b
  x_j = LN(x_j; F)
  logits_j = x_j @ transpose(E), the scores for the token after position j.
LN(u; n) = (u - mean(u)) / sqrt(var(u) + 0.00001) * n.scale + n.shift, element by element, with the mean and population variance taken over the 1024 entries of u.
gelu here is the standard smooth approximation of u * Phi(u), which differs from it by at most 0.0005.
The model's top token is the one with the largest logit; a tie goes to the lowest token ID.

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
import pandas as pd

torch.set_num_threads(4)

def tensor(name):
    return torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(W[name]))

def effective_input(a, scale):
    a = scale[:, None] * a
    return a - a.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)

rows = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for l in range(24):
        qw = tensor(f"L{l}.qkv.W")
        ow = tensor(f"L{l}.out.W")
        scale = tensor(f"L{l}.norm1.scale")
        for h in range(16):
            s = slice(64*h, 64*(h+1))
            Q = effective_input(qw[:, s], scale)
            K = effective_input(qw[:, 1024+64*h:1024+64*(h+1)], scale)
            V = effective_input(qw[:, 2048+64*h:2048+64*(h+1)], scale)
            O = ow[s, :]
            ov_small = O @ V
            qk_small = K.T @ Q
            ov_eig = torch.linalg.eigvals(ov_small)
            qk_eig = torch.linalg.eigvals(qk_small)
            ov_norm = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(
                ((V.T @ V) * (O @ O.T)).sum(), min=0)).item()
            qk_norm = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(
                ((Q.T @ Q) * (K.T @ K)).sum(), min=0)).item()
            ov_trace = torch.trace(ov_small).item()
            qk_trace = torch.trace(qk_small).item()
            rows.append(dict(
                head=f"{l}.{h}", layer=l, h=h,
                ov_trace=ov_trace, ov_norm=ov_norm,
                ov_copy=ov_trace/(ov_norm+1e-12),
                ov_eig_balance=ov_trace/(ov_eig.abs().sum().item()+1e-12),
                ov_top_real=ov_eig.real.max().item(),
                qk_trace=qk_trace, qk_norm=qk_norm,
                qk_match=qk_trace/(qk_norm+1e-12),
                qk_eig_balance=qk_trace/(qk_eig.abs().sum().item()+1e-12)
            ))

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
pd.set_option("display.width", 180)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 60)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)
pd.set_option("display.float_format", lambda x: f"{x:.4f}")
print("Strongest positive value-output copying maps:")
print(df.sort_values("ov_copy", ascending=False).head(55).to_string(index=False))
print("\nStrongest query-key self-matching maps:")
print(df.sort_values("qk_match", ascending=False).head(20).to_string(index=False))
print("\nMost negative query-key self-matching maps:")
print(df.sort_values("qk_match").head(20).to_string(index=False))
print("\nLayer medians:")
print(df.groupby("layer")[["ov_norm","ov_copy","qk_norm","qk_match"]].median().to_string())
```
